claims.text: At high temperature, chromium preferentially diffuses and segregates to the surface of CoCrFeMnNi.
Surface-segregated chromium selectively oxidizes to form Cr2O3.
Cr2O3 has a compact structure and can provide superior oxidation resistance as an oxide barrier.
A continuous and adherent Cr2O3 surface layer limits external oxygen transport and thereby slows further oxidation.
Manganese has a higher affinity for oxygen and can preferentially diffuse to the surface of CrMnFeCoNi at elevated temperature.
Competition from manganese oxidation can suppress or mask Cr2O3-scale formation.
Manganese competition in Cr-lean alloys produces non-protective or spall-prone oxides.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will form a thin, uniform, continuous, and protective Cr2O3 scale during oxidation at 1000–1100 °C in air.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will exhibit lower oxidation mass gain than a Cr-lean variant.
A Cr-lean CoCrFeMnNi variant will form more discontinuous or mixed oxides, including more manganese oxides, than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The Cr-lean variant will oxidize more rapidly because chromium segregation is inadequate to establish a protective scale.
Oxidation rate in CrMnFeCoNi increases with increasing oxygen partial pressure.
Lower oxygen partial pressure can produce an extremely thin scale and shift manganese oxidation to higher temperature.
The proposed chromium-segregation mechanism applies specifically to isothermal oxidation in air at 1000–1100 °C.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes preferential outward diffusion to Cr, whereas the cited same-system evidence explicitly identifies Mn as the element that preferentially diffuses to the surface because of its greater oxygen affinity.

The proposed and predicted mediator is a continuous Cr2O3 layer, but the cited air-oxidation record reports that Cr2O3 was not detected and instead associates its absence with continued Mn diffusion and Mn3O4 formation. The evidence is at 950 °C rather than the proposed 1000–1100 °C, so the temperature ranges are not identical.

The boundary states that the hypothesis applies to equiatomic alloys, while the required baseline is a deliberately non-equiatomic Cr-lean variant. This creates a scope mismatch for interpreting the controlled comparison.
